primitives.name: Pace Calibration Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: 46 WALTER CAMP'S BOOK OF COLLEGE SPORTS half —sometimes a 300; on occasional afternoons, the 220-yard dashes,—of course with a rest between; and once a week, a quarter on time.
primitives.assumptions: Training intervals are uniformly distributed with fixed recovery periods; performance scales linearly with distance up to threshold.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Exceeds 300-yard interval limits without adequate recovery leads to pacing degradation.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian model uses pace kernel outputs to predict race-time distributions based on training logs.
layer2.telemetry: Average lap times per distance segment during interval runs

primitives.name: Temporal Pacing Duality
primitives.verbatim_quote: With the increased distance comes that increased value of a knowledge of pace which the runner must acquire from daily running under the watch, until he knows what time he is making.
primitives.assumptions: Velocity profile is deterministic within training constraints; pacing accuracy improves with repetition.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure to calibrate v(t) results in premature fatigue or late-race slowdown.

layer2.mapping: GSE state machine encodes temporal duality as discrete pacing states with transition probabilities.

primitives.name: Gait Consistency Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: But he must not (any more than the 220 man) get an idea that he can run the first part of his race easy and then finish fast.
primitives.assumptions: Gait remains stable unless externally perturbed; inconsistent pacing causes energy inefficiency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Δg > 0.1 leads to metabolic imbalance and suboptimal race execution.

layer2.mapping: GSI constraint engine enforces gait stability via variance minimization in kinematic traces.
layer2.telemetry: Stride frequency and cadence consistency metrics
